newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka to free ship after search.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka to free ship after search.

text.p: Sri Lankan authorities found nothing suspicious aboard a Cyprus-registered freighter detained off a rebel stronghold, and plan to release the ship and its 28 Cuban crew members, a navy spokesman said on Tuesday.
"We searched the ship after she was detained because she was making suspicious movements," the spokesman told Reuters. "Nothing suspicious was found and we're going to release her."

He said the 1,674-tonne Caribbean Queen was detained on Sunday after it made suspicious movements, failed to answer radio calls and ignored warning shots fired by air force planes while the vessel was in Sri Lankan territorial waters near a Tamil rebel stronghold.
"We had intelligence that there was a suspicious ship off Mullaitivu (on the east coast) that could be unloading arms for the LTTE (Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam)," he said.
The spokesman said he could not immediately say how the crew had explained their actions.
Cuba's ambassador to Colombo was flown to Trincomalee, where the ship was detained, but embassy officials in the capital refused to comment on the case.
The ship's captain had asked to enter the port for repairs, the navy spokesman said, adding that the ship would be released after the repairs.
A Defence Ministry statement on Monday said the ship originally reported having engine trouble. The vessel was fired on and forced to stop when it suddenly started its engines and tried to sail away.
None of the freighter's 28 Cuban crew members were hurt, military officials said.

The military first became suspicions because of the presence of a small boat near the freighter, the Defence Ministry said. The boat was blown up with a rocket fired from a Pucara aircraft when it ignored warning shots and tried to flee.

Mi-24 helicopter gunships joined the Pucara when Colombo shipping authorities could not confirm statements by the ship's crew that the vessel was the Caribbean Queen, sailing from India to Colombo for fuel and provisions, the statement said.

The navy and air force have recently stepped up patrols around this Indian Ocean island to intercept ships ferrying arms to the LTTE, which is fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the north and east.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year.
